summary: William Jones (1746–1794) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Harrow School, Middle Temple, and University College, Oxford, and under Mirza I'tisam-ud-Din, Ramchandra, and Rāmalocana. He served as Chief Justice at Fort William and founded The Asiatic Society in 1784.

William L. Ames worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He earned an M.S. from Caltech and a Ph.D. from the University of Washington under Collett Cox and David Seyfort Ruegg, later holding posts at JFK University, Caltech, and UW.

William M. Bodiford is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Kansas, Tsukuba, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He taught at Davidson and Iowa before a long career at UCLA (1992–2021).

William M. Gorvine is a scholar in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Connecticut College and an M.A. and Ph.D. (2006) from the University of Virginia, where he studied under David Germano, among other faculty.
William P. Chu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, earning an M.A. in 2006 under the doctoral supervision of Robert E. Buswell Jr.

William Price (1780–1830) was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He taught oriental languages at Netherstone House Seminary and served as Professor of Hindústaní at Fort William College (~1813–1830).

William R. Hutchison (1930–2005) was a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University. He held posts at American University (~1959–1966), Harvard University (from 1968), Yale, Hunter College, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

William R. LaFleur (1936–2010) specialized in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Calvin University, Michigan, and Chicago, he held posts at Princeton (~1971–1978), UCLA (~1978–1990), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1990–2010).

William Rainey Harper (1856–1906) was a linguist who studied at Muskingum and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Denison, Baptist Union Theological Seminary, and Yale, and served as president of the University of Chicago (1891–1906) and Bradley University (~1897–1906).

William Roxburgh (1751–1815) worked in Indology and botany. He studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh and Marischal College, Aberdeen. His career included serving at Madras Medical Service, Samalkot Experimental Farm, and as superintendent of the Indian Botanic Garden from 1793.

William S. Waldron is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He conducted research at Otani University and held an appointment at Middlebury College (attested 2003).

William Stede (1882–1958) was an Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an editor for the Pali Text Society (~1916–1958) and held an academic post at SOAS, University of London (~1928–1949).

William Van Gordon is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He founded the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research and served as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University (attested 2015).

William Ward (1769–1823) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Ewood Hall Academy under John Fawcett in 1797, co-founded Serampore College in 1818, and served as a missionary at the Serampore Mission from 1799 to 1823.

William Wilson Hunter (1840–1900) was a scholar of Indology and history. He studied at Glasgow, Paris, and Bonn, served in the Indian Civil Service (~1862–1887), and was vice-chancellor of the University of Calcutta in 1886.

William Woodville Rockhill (1854–1914) was a scholar in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr, and under Léon Feer and Philippe Édouard Foucaux between ~1877 and 1884.

William Wright (1830–1889) was a linguist who studied at St Andrews, Halle-Wittenberg, and Leiden. He held professorships of Arabic at University College London, Trinity College Dublin, and the University of Cambridge (1870–1889), and worked at the British Museum.

Willibald Kirfel (1885–1964) was an Indologist. He completed his Ph.D. and Habilitation at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked as a librarian at Bonn University Library before becoming an ordinary professor at the University of Bonn in 1922.

Wilt L. Idema (born 1944) is a Sinologist. He earned his degrees at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé and served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and Harvard University (2000–2013).

Winfred P. Lehmann (1916–2007) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1938–1941) and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).
